title: Verify a snapshot by restoring it
summary: Distinguish a committed local database, a copied snapshot and an independently readable restore.
objectives: Check an isolated SQLite backup by reopening its destination.
Report the restored revision instead of claiming it is automatically current.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.basis: Explains database snapshots through the backup interface; destination contents and revision are independently checked here.

sections.title: A tool installation is not recovery evidence
paragraphs: Use the database backup API to create a synthetic snapshot, then open the destination separately and read its record. Do not copy a live database file and assume its WAL is included.
A cloud-backed filesystem, a local transaction, a cache and a backup destination are different capabilities. Remote storage must not silently become the canonical database.

sections.title: State exactly what was restored
paragraphs: After making the snapshot, change the source revision. The reopened snapshot still contains its earlier revision; label that revision explicitly.

Production recovery must separately cover attachments, encryption and key recovery, interrupted uploads, corruption, retention and a restore drill. An unavailable provider does not mean local records were erased.

exercise.instruction: Run the selected-knowledge exercises with pnpm test.
exercise.expected: Assert the documented result and its negative boundary; no external operation is performed.

limitations: Uses a temporary local SQLite database only. It does not test power loss, encrypted bundles, external storage, replication or production recovery.
